Now, in order to be considered for investment, these bonds must have a certain level of security. For example, a government bond is considered “low risk” because the government will repay the debt when it’s due, while a company bond is considered “high risk” because it’s possible that the company may not be able to repay the debt. Investors typically prefer low risk bonds, so high risk company bonds may not sell very well.

That being said, bonds do come in different types. Bonds can be categorized by the issuer and the type of bond you’re investing in. Issuer refers to the company or fund that sells the bond, and there are hundreds of different issuer types. 

There are three main categories of bond – government, corporate, and mortgage-backed bonds.

Government bonds are issued by governments, typically the government of the nation the bond is issued in. Government bonds usually guarantee that the debt will be repaid to the investor, so they’re considered “low risk”. They’re often bought in large quantities by investors, and they tend to be very liquid.

Corporate bonds are issued by companies to raise capital. When a company issues a bond, the debt is essentially a loan. Companies usually expect some share of the profits to go back to the bondholder, in the form of dividends, but not all of their profits are distributed that way. Companies usually have some level of creditworthiness, since they are essentially lending money to other people, so they can usually expect to repay the debt.

Mortgage-backed bonds are bonds issued in connection with the underlying loans associated with mortgages (meaning the bond issuer buys the debt on those mortgages). The debt on the bond is usually associated with a group of mortgages. Sometimes this means you’re buying a bond that originated from some specific type of mortgages. In some cases mortgage-backed bonds do guarantee repayment, but they don’t always guarantee repayment. Also, mortgage-backed bonds typically come from the United States and have an AAA credit rating.

By buying bonds through these channels, investors are often getting into a company’s bond directly. Some bond funds are structured to take advantage of this, buying bonds that correspond to the companies you own in your own mutual funds. Dash of salt

Oil for frying

Method:
